blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Large language models (LLMs) have become increasingly capable problem solvers, but being able to solve a problem is not the same as being able to teach it. Existing approaches to training LLMs as teachers rely on demonstrations, preference data, or predefined pedagogical criteria that specify what good teaching looks like. However, these signals are often not grounded in individual student learning outcomes, where effective teaching strategies can vary substantially across learners.
To address this, we introduce Sherpa 1 1 1 Named after the Sherpa people, renowned Himalayan mountaineering guides, our framework aims to enable language models to help people reach new heights through learning. , a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework that instantiates multiple student archetypes with LLMs conditioned on distinct learning preferences and trains a teacher model to adapt its instruction by directly maximizing their learning outcomes.
Teacher LLMs trained with Sherpa improve instructed students’ performance across all archetypes by an average of 20.5 percentage points.
Under MathTutorBench’s evaluation, Sherpa raises the overall pedagogy score from 52.5% to 79.2%, indicating better teaching responses.
Our human studies show that the trained teacher is preferred over the base model in 79.6% of pairwise comparisons.
Together, Sherpa trains LLM teachers to adapt to diverse simulated students and become better aligned with human teachers, paving the road towards AI tutors teaching real students. 2 2 2 Code and model are available at https://github.com/SALT-NLP/Sherpa .

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Large language models (LLMs) have advanced rapidly, achieving strong capabilities in mathematical reasoning and code generation ( Yang et al., 2024 ; Hui et al., 2024 ) . Solving a problem, however, is different from teaching someone else to solve it. Srinivasa et al. (2025) finds that none of the 16 evaluated frontier models scores above 56% against its expert-written tutoring rubrics, while Macina et al. (2025) shows that strong problem-solving ability does not directly translate into effective teaching. This gap matters for human learners: studies of general-purpose AI use have raised concerns that receiving effective task assistance does not necessarily translate into learning, and may even reduce cognitive engagement or subsequent independent performance ( Kosmyna et al., 2025 ; Bastani et al., 2025 ) . LLMs may thus erode learners’ agency rather than help preserve it. Developing models that help people learn to think and solve problems independently is therefore increasingly important, beyond improving individual dimensions of teaching skill.
blocks.zh: 大型语言模型(LLMs)已经迅速进步,在数学推理和代码生成方面实现了强大的能力(杨等,2024;Hui等,2024.). 然而,解决问题不同于教别人解决问题。 Srinivasa等人(2025年)发现,16个被评价的前沿模型中没有一个比其专家写作的导师分数超过56%,而Macina等人(2025年)则显示强大的解决问题能力并没有直接转化为有效的教学. 对人类学习者来说,这一差距很重要:对通用AI的使用的研究引起了人们的关切,即接受有效任务援助不一定转化为学习,甚至可能减少认知接触或随后的独立表现(Kosmyna等,2025;Bastani等,2025)。 因此,LLMS可能会侵蚀学习者的能力,而不是帮助维护学习者的能力。 因此,除了提高教学技能的个人层面外,发展有助于人们独立思考和解决问题的模式日益重要。

blocks.en: One approach to AI-assisted learning is to build educational systems around existing LLMs, injecting human-designed pedagogical strategies through prompts or external scaffolding ( Chen et al., 2024 ; Puech et al., 2024 ) . Such systems can provide useful instructional structure, but they primarily shape the model’s behavior at inference time. To develop teaching as an intrinsic capability of the model itself , a growing body of work instead trains LLMs specifically as teachers. Supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization came first, but they rely on the quality and coverage of instructional demonstrations or preference data ( Macina et al., 2023 ; Scarlatos et al., 2025 ) . More recent work has turned to reinforcement learning so that teachers can learn from their own interactions with simulated students ( Dinucu-Jianu et al., 2025 ; Chang et al., 2026 ) . Yet these approaches share a fundamental limitation: their training signals encode predefined notions of what good teaching looks like, rather than being grounded directly in diverse students’ learning outcomes. In practice, students differ in their preferences and needs, and effective teaching cannot be fully specified without accounting for this heterogeneity.
blocks.zh: 人工智能辅助学习的一个办法是围绕现有法学硕士建立教育系统,通过提示或外部脚手架注入人设计的教学战略(Chen等,2024;Puech等,2024)。 这种系统可以提供有用的指导结构,但它们主要在推断时间塑造模型的行为. 为了发展教学作为模式本身的内在能力,越来越多的工作将专门培训法学硕士。 监督的微调和偏好优化首先出现,但它们依赖于教学演示或偏好数据的质量和覆盖面(Macina等,2023;Scarlatos等,2025.). 最近的工作转向强化学习,使教师能够从自己与模拟学生的互动中学习(Dinucu-Jianu等,2025;Chan等,2026)。 然而,这些方法有一个根本的局限性:它们的培训信号编码了好的教学是什么样子的预先定义的概念,而不是直接基于学生的学习结果。 在实践中,学生的偏好和需要不同,如果不考虑这种异同性,就无法充分规定有效的教学.

blocks.en: To close this gap, we introduce Sherpa , a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework that trains a teacher to improve student task-solving across diverse student archetypes. In this work, we train through interactions with language-model students and use pairwise comparisons from human teachers to assess whether the learned teaching behavior aligns with human judgments of effective teaching. Rather than predefining what constitutes good teaching, Sherpa separates pedagogical specification from teacher optimization: diverse instructional needs are instantiated on the student side, while the teacher is optimized based on student improvement. Each teaching episode follows a preparation–tutoring–testing cycle: given a problem, the teacher first prepares a solution, tutors the student over multiple turns of interaction, and is rewarded based on the student’s improvement at test time. However, student models exhibit similar preferences for instructional strategies even after prompting or across model families, making them insufficiently diverse as archetypes for our environment. We therefore design a gating mechanism that makes instructional strategies consequential: guidance that meets the student’s preference passes the gate and is forwarded to the student backbone model to elicit substantive reasoning, whereas incompatible guidance is blocked and receives feedback requesting more appropriate instruction. The teacher must therefore infer each student’s needs from interaction and adapt its teaching accordingly. In this way, Sherpa allows diverse teaching behaviors to emerge while keeping the optimization objective simple and outcome-based.
blocks.zh: 为了缩小这一差距,我们引入了Shelpa, 一个多回合强化学习框架, 培训一位教师, 在这项工作中,我们通过与语言模范学生的互动来培训,并使用人类教师的对等比较来评估所学的教学行为是否与人类对有效教学的判断一致. 舍尔巴不是预先确定什么是好的教学,而是将教学的规格与教师优化区分开来:不同的教学需求在学生方面被即时化,而教师则在学生改进的基础上被优化. 每集教学都遵循一个准备-测试-测试周期:鉴于一个问题,老师首先准备一个解决方案,辅导学生进行多轮互动,并根据学生在测试时的改进情况给予奖励。 然而,即使在激励或跨模范家庭之后,学生模式对教学战略也表现出类似的偏好,使它们作为我们环境的典型类型不够多样化。 因此,我们设计了一个使教学策略产生结果的取景机制:满足学生偏好的指导通过大门,并被传送到学生骨干模型,以引出实质性推理,而不相容的指导则被阻断并收到反馈,要求进行更适当的教学。 因此,教师必须从互动中推断每个学生的需求,并相应调整教学。 这样,舍尔巴允许不同的教学行为出现,同时保持了优化客观的简单和基于结果.

blocks.en:
We identify six important student learning preferences from education literature and initiate corresponding student archetypes using Qwen3-1.7B ( Yang et al., 2025 ) as the backbone model, and train a Qwen3-8B ( Yang et al., 2025 ) teacher to help students on MATH problems ( Hendrycks et al., 2021 ) . Sherpa improves final test accuracy across all student archetypes, including those unseen during training, increasing average student performance by 20.5 percentage points. Moreover, these gains transfer to unseen data and settings: on MathTutorBench ( Macina et al., 2025 ) , our training raises the overall pedagogy score from 52.5% to 79.2%, outperforming PedagogicalRL ( Dinucu-Jianu et al., 2025 ) on all four pedagogical metrics and achieving the highest average pedagogy score among the evaluated models. Our human study shows that the trained teacher is preferred over the base model in 79.6% of pairwise comparisons.
Finally, we compare different student archetype designs and show that our design effectively elicits the student behaviors needed for our training environment compared to baselines. We further ablate different reward designs and show that a simple optimization objective substantially improves generalization.
blocks.zh:
我们从教育文献中找出了6个重要的学生学习偏好,并启动相应的以Qune3-1.7B(杨等,2025年)为骨干模式的学生型,并培养出一名Qune3-8B(杨等,2025年)教师来帮助学生解决MATH问题(Hendrycks等,2021年). 舍尔巴提高包括培训期间所未见的学生等所有学生型的期末测试精度,使学生平均成绩提高了20.5个百分点. 此外,这些收益转移到无形的数据和环境中:在MathTutor Bench(Macina等,2025年)上,我们的培训将总体教学学得分从52.5%提高到79.2%,在所有四个教学指标上成绩优于教学RL(Dinucu-Jianu等,2025年),并在被评价的模型中实现了最高的平均教学学得分。 我们的人类研究表明,79.6%的对等比较中,训练有素的教师优于基准模型。
最后,我们比较了不同的学生型式设计,并表明我们的设计有效地引领了学生在训练环境上所需的行为与基线相比. 我们进一步降低不同的奖励设计,并表明简单的优化目标可大大地改进概括。

blocks.en: 2 How to Train an Adaptive Teacher LLM?
blocks.zh: 2 如何培训适应性教师 LLM?

blocks.en: Figure 1: Overview of our framework. The teacher interacts with student archetypes through preparation, tutoring, and testing, and receives a reward for tutoring based on the student’s improvement. The student archetype is implemented by a backbone model with a gating mechanism.
blocks.zh: 图1:我们框架概览。 教师通过准备、辅导和测试与学生的型号互动,并根据学生的改进获得辅导奖励。 学生型由具有取景机制的骨干模型来实施.

blocks.en:
As shown in Figure 1 , our framework trains an adaptive teacher LLM through interaction with diverse student archetypes. The teaching process follows a classroom cycle with three stages, which together constitute a teaching episode: preparation , in which the teacher prepares the material; tutoring , in which the teacher chats with the student; and testing , in which the student completes a test.
Based on this design, we optimize the teacher via multi-turn reinforcement learning. We first formulate the problem (§ 2.1 ), then describe our student archetype design (§ 2.2 ), and finally present our teacher training method (§ 2.3 ).

基于这一设计,我们通过多回合强化学习,优化了老师. 我们首先提出问题(第2.1节),然后描述我们的学生原型设计(第2.2节),最后介绍我们的教师培训方法(第2.3节)。

blocks.en: 2.2 Student Archetype
blocks.zh: 2.2 学生考古类型

blocks.en: To design student archetypes with different latent variables z z that genuinely require different guidance strategies, we propose two principles:
blocks.zh: 为了设计具有不同潜在变量z z z,真正需要不同指导策略的学生型,我们提出两项原则:

blocks.en: 1. Selective: student improvement should depend on whether the teacher’s instruction meets the demands represented by z z . 2. Informative: student replies should reflect the preference represented by z z .
blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 选择性:学生的改善应该取决于教师的教学是否符合z z 的要求。 2. 资料:学生的答复应反映z z 所代表的偏好。

blocks.en: Selective: student improvement should depend on whether the teacher’s instruction meets the demands represented by z z .
blocks.zh: 选择性:学生的改善应该取决于教师的教学是否符合z z 的要求。

blocks.en: Informative: student replies should reflect the preference represented by z z .
blocks.zh: 资料性:学生的答复应反映z z所代表的偏好.

blocks.en: Together, these principles make the student’s latent demands both consequential for learning and inferable from interaction. Satisfying both, however, is challenging. Existing approaches often start from models capable of solving the target problems and use prompting or unlearning to induce different student behaviors ( Scarlatos et al., 2026 ; Song et al., 2026 ) . Such students may still benefit from generic explanations regardless of their assigned needs, while knowledge targeted by unlearning can remain accessible ( Lynch et al., 2024 ; Thaker et al., 2025 ) . Directly training models to mimic student behaviors can instead lead to excessive error imitation and degraded problem-solving ability ( Sonkar et al., 2024a ) , complicating the measurement of teaching effectiveness.
blocks.zh: 这些原则共同使学生的潜在要求既影响学习,也影响互动。 然而,满足双方的要求具有挑战性。 现有方法往往从能够解决目标问题的模型入手,并使用激励或不学习来诱发不同的学生行为(Scarlatos等,2026;Song等,2026). 这些学生仍可从一般解释中受益,而不管他们被分配到何种需要,而非学习对象的知识仍可获得(Lynch等人,2024年;Thaker等人,2025年)。 直接训练模型来模仿学生的行为反而会导致过量地模仿错误并降低解决问题的能力(Sonkar等,2024a),使教学效果的测量复杂化.

blocks.en: In Sherpa , we instead use a weak model that cannot solve the problem unaided as the student backbone. This makes learning gains easier to attribute to tutoring, but the weaker model is also less reliable at expressing distinct behaviors through prompting alone. We therefore use gates to control which teacher instructions reach the student backbone. Specifically, we decompose adaptive teaching into two components: providing useful guidance and matching that guidance to the student’s latent demands, and implement it with a guidance gate and an adaptive gate .
blocks.zh: 在舍尔帕,我们使用一个弱的模型 无法解决问题 不作为学生的骨干。 这使得学习增益更容易归属于辅导,但较弱的模型在通过单独提示表达不同行为时也不太可靠. 因此,我们利用大门来控制 老师的指示到达学生的骨干。 具体地说,我们把适应性教学分为两个部分:提供有用的指导,并将指导与学生的潜在需求相匹配,并以指导门和适应性门加以实施。

blocks.en: Guidance Gate. We view guidance as helping the student make progress while leaving room for the student to think. A teacher model can instead solve the problem entirely, allowing the student to reproduce it without reasoning. To prevent this shortcut, we require the teacher to guide the student toward the solution without disclosing the final answer. Prior work uses LLM judges to detect answer leakage or assess teaching quality ( Dinucu-Jianu et al., 2025 ) , but broad judgments may either miss localized disclosure or penalize legitimate guidance such as intermediate calculations and worked steps. We therefore make the criterion explicit: the guidance gate uses an LLM checker to determine whether each teacher instruction reveals the ground-truth final answer. Instructions that do so are blocked; intermediate reasoning and partial solutions remain allowed. This design permits substantive guidance while leaving the student to work out the final answer.
blocks.zh: 指导门. 我们认为,指导有助于学生取得进展,同时为学生留下思考的余地。 教师模式可以完全解决问题,让学生在不推理的情况下复制. 为了防止这个捷径,我们要求老师在不透露最终答案的情况下引导学生走向解决方案. 先前的工作利用LLM法官来检测答案漏出或评估教学质量(Dinucu-Jianu等,2025年),但广义的判断可能错失了局部的披露,或者惩罚诸如中间计算和工作步骤等合法指导. 因此,我们明确标准:指导门使用一个LLM检查器来确定每个教师指示是否揭示了地面-真实的最后答案。 这样做的指令被屏蔽;中间推理和部分解决方案仍然被允许. 这种设计允许实质性指导,同时让学生去研究最后的答案.

blocks.en: Adaptive Gate. Avoiding answer disclosure does not by itself guarantee adaptive teaching. If every student archetype benefits from the same explanation, the teacher has no incentive to infer individual needs. We therefore assign students different preferences for teaching strategies drawn from widely studied pedagogical interventions:
blocks.zh: 适应出道口. 避免披露答案本身并不能保障适应性教学。 如果每个学生的原型都受益于同样的解释,那么老师就没有动力推断个人需要. 因此,我们从广泛学习的教学措施中为学生提供不同的教学战略:

blocks.en: We first describe how we roll out the teaching episode from the teacher’s perspective and how we optimize the teacher based on student improvement.

blocks.en:
Teaching Episode (i) Preparation. The teacher privately solves the assigned problem and retains a solution draft as background knowledge, just like human teachers prepare a problem’s solution and underlying reasoning before teaching it. For LLM teachers, particularly small models, keeping the solution draft available throughout tutoring helps reduce drift as the dialogue grows and improves teaching performance. We provide the detailed comparison in Appendix C.1 . (ii) Tutoring. The teacher initiates the dialogue with a student archetype, with the problem and the solution draft at the beginning of the teacher context.
At each turn, the teacher generates a complete response y t ∼ π θ ( ⋅ ∣ C t T ) y_{t}\sim\pi_{\theta}(\cdot\mid C_{t}^{T}) , consisting of private reasoning and a student-visible instruction a t a_{t} .
The private part allows the teacher to reason freely without being constrained by student preferences.
After receiving student reply o t o_{t} , the teacher context is always updated: C t + 1 T = C t T ⊕ ( a t , o t ) C_{t+1}^{T}=C_{t}^{T}\oplus(a_{t},o_{t}) .
We set a turn budget for tutoring, while the teacher may also end the tutoring earlier, mirroring the conclusion of a lesson. (iii) Testing. After tutoring, we test the student by providing C H S C_{H}^{S} together with the original problem, and asking it to produce a complete solution. We estimate accuracy through repeated testing.
To measure the student’s unaided performance, we evaluate the same student model without providing the interaction history accumulated during tutoring.

blocks.en: Student Archetypes. We instantiate seven student archetypes: six with distinct preferences enforced by their respective adaptive gates, and one without preference (None, Non.). The descriptions and names below distinguish them by their preferences. Our model is trained on four of these archetypes (None, Non.; Attempt, Att.; Subgoal, Sub.; Contrast, Ctr.), making them in-distribution (ID) and the remaining three (Causal, Cau.; Step, Stp.; and Verification, Ver.) for out-of-distribution (OOD) evaluation. Detailed descriptions of the student preferences are provided in Section 2.2 .

blocks.en: Problems Filtering. We focus on mathematics, where teacher models possess substantial task knowledge and student answers can be easily judged. Our problems come from MATH ( Hendrycks et al., 2021 ) , with filtering to remove less teachable cases: problems beyond the teacher’s capabilities and those the student can already solve unaided. Therefore, we select problems for which the teacher has relevant knowledge and the student has room to improve. This filtering retains 759 training and 528 evaluation problems from the corresponding dataset splits.

blocks.en: Results. As shown in Table 1 , Sherpa DP achieves an overall test accuracy of 69.0%, outperforming the untrained backbone, PedagogicalRL, and Sherpa NP on every student archetype. Sherpa NP also improves on the untrained backbone, raising overall test accuracy from 48.6% to 52.0%, comparable to PedagogicalRL’s 52.7%. This demonstrates the effectiveness of using student improvement to guide teacher training. Furthermore, Sherpa DP performs substantially better than Sherpa NP across student archetypes, demonstrating the importance of diverse student archetypes in training. The gains in accuracy differ across archetypes, indicating that improvements do not transfer equally across them (Causal: 55.1% to 77.1%, Step: 40.6% to 51.8%). Additional results on different student backbone models and multiple training seeds are provided in Appendices C.2.3 and C.2.4 .

Sherpa NP也改进了未经训练的骨干,将总体测试精度从48.6%提高到52.0%,与教学RL的52.7%相当. 这表明利用学生改进指导教师培训的有效性。 此外,Shelpa DP在学生的形而上学方面表现大大优于Shelpa NP,这表明不同学生形而上学在培训中的重要性。 不同型号的精度提高不尽相同,表明改进在它们之间的转移并不相等(考萨尔:55.1%至77.1%,步道:40.6%至51.8%)。 附录C.2.3和C.2.4提供了不同学生骨干模型和多种培训种子的其他结果。

Setup To test whether our gains generalize beyond our setting, we evaluate on MathTutorBench ( Macina et al., 2025 ) , a teacher-grounded mathematics tutoring benchmark.
It covers math expertise (Problem Solving, PS; Socratic Questioning, SQ), student understanding (Solution Correctness, SC; Mistake Location, ML; Mistake Correction, MC), and teacher response generation (Scaffolding, Scaf.; Instruction Following, IF; and harder variants Scaf.-H and IF-H). Because the last category most directly measures teaching quality, we summarize it with Pedagogy Average (Ped. Avg.), the mean of its four tasks.
Evaluation details are in Appendix B.3 .

blocks.en: Results Table 2 shows that the model trained with Sherpa also performs well on MathTutorBench, especially on teacher response generation. Sherpa DP achieves the highest Pedagogy Average among the evaluated models, at 79.2%, compared with 52.5% for the untrained backbone and 63.2% for PedagogicalRL, and improves on all four constituent metrics. Training raises instruction-following win rates from 74.0% to 90.3% in the standard setting and from 70.6% to 87.2% in the hard setting. Scaffolding scores also increase from 33.1% to 72.0% and from 32.4% to 67.3%, respectively. These gains indicate that training improves both adherence to students’ instructional requests and the ability to provide guidance that supports their progress. Meanwhile, mistake-location accuracy declines across all trained teachers, and most also regress on Socratic questioning, suggesting a side effect of specific training for teaching. Nonetheless, Sherpa DP retains higher mistake-location accuracy than PedagogicalRL (30.3% versus 18.7%).

For each conversation, we create four variants of the final student response by injecting explicit preferences: two ID preferences (subgoal decomposition and contrastive comparison) and two OOD preferences (causal justification and error anticipation).
For each context, Qwen3-8B and Sherpa DP each generate a short tutor response. We then recruit 96 high school teachers via Prolific 4 4 4 https://www.prolific.com/ to answer “ Which response teaches the student better? ” and explain their choice. Results Teachers substantially prefer our model: it receives 728 judgments versus 187 for the base model, corresponding to a 79.6% win rate excluding ties. The advantage holds across all four preferences (75.6-85.5%), including the two preferences unseen during training. Moreover, 87 of 96 teachers favor Sherpa DP more often across their judgments, and majority voting prefers it on 270 of 320 response pairs versus 34 for the base model. Figure 2 illustrates a representative comparison.
Participants’ explanations most often attribute this preference to better guidance tailored to the student’s requested approach, and sometimes to better identification and correction of mistakes. A minority prefer the base response when they find our explanations potentially overwhelming, suggesting that improved adaptivity can occasionally come at the cost of simplicity.

blocks.en: 3.4 Evaluating the Training Design
blocks.zh: 3.4 国家 评估培训设计

blocks.en:
Student Archetypes for Teacher Training We evaluate and compare our student archetype design with prompted students , which are given the same six preferences explicitly in their prompts.
In Figure 3 , we pair a GPT-5.6-Luna teacher using one of six fixed teaching strategies with a student having one of six preferences, yielding a 6 × 6 6\times 6 matrix for each design; diagonal cells correspond to matched teacher-student pairs. Selectivity is measured by differentiated improvement, where a strong design should show higher values along the diagonal. Informativeness is measured by differentiated complaint rate: when instruction is unsuitable, students return a prescribed complaint, so matched pairs should exhibit lower complaint rates.
We find that prompted students show neither a clear diagonal advantage in improvement nor consistently lower complaint rates along the diagonal.
On the other hand, our archetypes show both desired properties: improvement is concentrated along the diagonal, while complaint rates are lower for matched pairs.
blocks.zh:
师范学生考古类型 我们评价学生的原型设计,
在图3中,我们使用六个固定教学策略之一的GPT-5.6-Luna教师与一个有六个偏好的学生对一对,每次设计产生一个6×6 6\6的矩阵;对角细胞对应的是匹配的师生对等. 选择性通过有区别的改进来衡量,其中强度的设计应显示对角线上较高的值. 信息性以不同的投诉率衡量:当教学不适当时,学生会退回规定的投诉,因此匹配的对子应显示较低的投诉率.
我们发现,促使学生在改善方面既没有明显的对角优势,也没有在对角线沿线一贯降低投诉率。
另一方面,我们的原型显示了两种理想的特性:改进集中在对角线上,而对应对子的投诉率更低.

blocks.en:
Training Teachers through Student Improvement Sherpa uses improvements in students’ task-solving performance as a training signal for teachers. To examine how additional penalties affect teaching performance, we compare penalty magnitudes of 0.25 and 0.5 for failures of either gate.
The results show that adding gate penalties substantially affects teaching performance. On held-out MathTutorBench (Figure 4 ), performance across all four pedagogical dimensions declines as the penalty increases, with Pedagogy Average dropping from 79.2% without gate penalties to 70.6% with a penalty of 0.25 and 66.0% with a penalty of 0.5. We additionally evaluate these variants on the main student archetypes. A small penalty leaves overall performance largely unchanged, whereas a larger penalty markedly reduces performance, including generalization to OOD archetypes. These results suggest that adding penalties based on predefined criteria harms generalization, whereas training based on student improvement allows broader teaching capabilities to emerge. Further experimental details and comparisons with other methods using predefined criteria are provided in Appendix C.4 .
blocks.zh:
通过学生改进Shelpa培训教师,将改进学生的任务解决表现作为教师的培训信号。 为了审查额外处罚如何影响教学业绩,我们比较了两个门的故障的处罚等级为0.25和0.5。
结果显示,加加入门处罚严重影响了教学业绩。 在被搁置的MathTutor Bench(图4)中,所有四个教学层面的成绩都随着处罚的增加而下降,平均教学率从79.2%没有门类处罚下降到70.6%,惩罚为0.25%和66.0%,惩罚为0.5。 我们额外评估了这些变体 在主要的学生型。 小的处罚使总体表现基本保持不变,而较大的处罚会显著地降低表现,包括被概括为OOD型. 这些结果表明,根据预先确定的标准增加处罚不利于普遍化,而以学生改进为基础的培训则可以产生更广泛的教学能力。 附录C.4提供了进一步的试验细节并使用预先界定的标准与其他方法进行比较。

blocks.en: 4 Related Work
blocks.zh: 4 相关工作

blocks.en: Prior work has developed benchmarks and interaction frameworks for evaluating and supporting teaching. MathTutorBench and TutorBench assess pedagogical skills beyond problem solving, revealing limitations in understanding students and providing effective guidance ( Macina et al., 2025 ; Srinivasa et al., 2025 ) . LongTutor extends evaluation to diagnosis and adaptive instruction grounded in learning histories ( Li et al., 2026 ) . System-level approaches introduce pedagogical structure around LLM backbones through explicit strategy steering ( Puech et al., 2024 ) , course planning and reflection ( Chen et al., 2024 ) , and instructional suggestions for human tutors ( Wang et al., 2024 ) . These studies establish evaluation foundations and demonstrate how structured interactions can support teaching. Our work addresses the complementary problem of training the underlying model to provide adaptive guidance.
blocks.zh: 先前的工作为评价和支持教学制定了基准和互动框架。 MathTutor Bench和Tutor Bench除了解决问题外,还评估教学技能,揭示在理解学生和提供有效指导方面的局限性(Macina等,2025;Srinivasa等,2025)。 LongTutor将评价扩展到基于学习历史的诊断和适应性教学(Li等,2026年)。 系统层面的方法通过明确的战略指导(Puech等,2024年),课程规划和思考(Chen等,2024年),以及对人类导师的指导建议(Wang等,2024年),围绕LLM主干线引入教学结构. 这些研究建立评价基础,并表明结构化的互动如何能支持教学。 我们的工作涉及培训基本模式以提供适应性指导的互补问题。

blocks.en: Supervised approaches develop teaching capabilities from human-authored or synthetic demonstrations, including MathDial, SocraticLM, and LearnLM ( Macina et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2024 ; LearnLM Team, 2024 ) . Preference optimization further shapes teaching behavior through comparisons of candidate responses ( Sonkar et al., 2024b ; Scarlatos et al., 2025 ) , making supervision dependent on the quality and coverage of collected or generated data. Online reinforcement learning allows teachers to learn from their own interactions with students. PedagogicalRL combines student success with leakage and helpfulness judgments ( Dinucu-Jianu et al., 2025 ) , while PEARL optimizes multiple explicitly defined pedagogical criteria ( Chang et al., 2026 ) . These approaches directly specify desirable teacher behavior through scoring rules. We instead treat these qualities as preferences of the learner. This formulation accommodates diverse teaching requirements through students and trains teachers based on student improvement.
blocks.zh: 监督方法从人类著作或合成演示中培养教学能力,包括MathDial、SocraticLM和LearnLM(Macina等,2023;Liu等,2024;LearnLM) Team, 2024 (英语). 优待优化通过比较考生反应进一步塑造了教学行为(Sonkar等,2024b;Scarlatos等,2025),使监督取决于所收集或生成的数据的质量和覆盖面. 在线强化学习使教师能够从自己与学生的互动中学习. 教学RL将学生的成功与渗漏和帮助判断结合起来(Dinucu-Jianu等,2025年),而PEARL则优化了多种明确定义的教学标准(Chan等,2026年). 这些方法通过评分规则直接指定了可取的老师行为. 相反,我们将这些品质视为学习者的偏好。 这种表述方式通过学生满足了不同的教学要求,并根据学生的改进对教师进行培训.

blocks.en:
Previous methods model learner responses and errors through prompting or fine-tuning, although mimicking student behavior does not by itself establish responsiveness to teacher instruction ( Scarlatos et al., 2026 ) . Training on student behavior can also impair a model’s knowledge and reasoning ( Sonkar et al., 2024a ) . Recent work, therefore, explicitly considers both behavioral fidelity and guidance responsiveness ( Yang et al., 2026 ) . Another approach uses unlearning to construct novice models and studies their subsequent relearning ( Song et al., 2026 ) . However, controlling knowledge through unlearning remains challenging: targeted information may remain accessible, while retained capabilities can be affected ( Lynch et al., 2024 ; Thaker et al., 2025 ) .
We intentionally build on a less capable student model and encode learner preferences through its adaptive gate, without additional parameter updates to mimic errors or suppress knowledge. Our goal is to construct student archetypes with distinct instructional needs while preserving the underlying model’s ability to benefit from guidance, as human students do. This ensures that improvements in student performance can serve as a reliable training signal for the teacher.
blocks.zh:
以往的方法通过提示或微调模拟学习者的反应和错误,虽然模仿学生的行为本身并不能确立对教师教学的响应性(Scarlatos等,2026年)。 学生行为训练也会损害模特的知识和推理(Sonkar等人,2024a)。 因此,最近的工作明确考虑了行为忠诚和引导反应(Yang等人,2026年)。 另一种方法利用不学习来构建新模式并研究其随后的再学习(Song等人,2026年)。 然而,通过不学习来控制知识仍然具有挑战性:目标信息可能仍然可用,而保留的能力可能受到影响(Lynch等人,2024年;Thaker等人,2025年)。
我们有意以能力较差的学生模式为基础,并通过其适应性门将学习者喜好编码,没有额外的参数更新来模仿错误或压制知识. 我们的目标是构建具有独特教学需要的学生型,同时保持基本模式像人类学生那样受益于指导的能力。 这保证了学生成绩的提高能够成为教师的可靠培训信号.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
In this work, to improve LLMs’ intrinsic teaching capabilities for diverse learning preferences, we developed Sherpa , a framework that learns adaptive guidance through interaction with student archetypes. Our framework cleanly separates teacher and student, using gating to instantiate different learning preferences and enable the teacher to learn adaptive guidance.
Instead of picking teaching metrics that capture diverse real-world needs, we train the teacher based on student improvement. Our results show that training improves student outcomes across different archetypes, with gains also extending to an external teaching benchmark. Moreover, human teachers compare our model’s responses with those of the base model and judge our model’s teaching responses to be substantially better. Further analysis demonstrates the importance of our student archetype design and the effectiveness and generalization benefits of training based on student improvement.
blocks.zh:
在这项工作中,为了提高LLMS的内在教学能力,我们开发了Shelpa,这个框架通过与学生原型的互动学习适应性指导。 我们的框架把老师和学生分开,用吉卜赛语来即兴发挥不同的学习喜好,使老师能够学习适应性指导.
我们没有选择能满足现实世界不同需要的教学指标,而是在学生改进的基础上培训教师。 我们的结果显示,培训提高了不同类型学生的成绩,成绩也扩大到外部教学基准。 此外,人类教师将我们模型的反应与基础模型的反应相比较,并判断我们模型的教学反应要好得多。 进一步的分析表明,我们的学生原型设计的重要性,以及基于学生改进的培训的有效性和普遍效益。

blocks.en: Looking ahead, the teacher-student separation allows us to refine the instructional needs represented by student archetypes independently of teacher training. Our evaluations show that Sherpa helps train LLM teachers that are more effective at supporting student models and better aligned with human teachers’ judgments, taking a further step toward using LLMs to directly support human students in real-world settings. Future work could consider more specific scenarios in which students have individual preferences, including combinations of our archetypes or beyond. Students may also be unaware of their own preferences, requiring teachers to gradually infer them through interaction. We hope this work provides a foundation for such efforts and helps translate the growing knowledge and reasoning capabilities of LLMs into teaching that strengthens humans’ understanding.
blocks.zh: 展望未来,师生分离使我们得以完善以学生传统型为代表的教学需求,独立于教师培训. 我们的评价显示,Shelpa帮助培训LLM教师,这些教师在支持学生模式方面更为有效,更符合人类教师的判断,在使用LLMs直接支持现实世界环境中的人类学生方面又迈出了一步. 今后的工作可以考虑学生有个人偏好的更具体的情况,包括我们传统类型或以外的组合。 学生也可能不知道自己的偏好,要求教师通过互动逐渐推断出自己的偏好. 我们希望这项工作为这些努力提供基础,并帮助将法学硕士不断增长的知识和推理能力转化为加强人类理解的教学。

blocks.en: B.1 Training and Generation Settings

blocks.en:
We use the 759 training and 528 evaluation problems retained by the MATH filtering procedure described in § 3.1 .
During training, we disable thinking for both the Qwen3-8B teacher and the Qwen3-1.7B student and use Qwen3-8B as the LLM judge for the guidance gate, adaptive gate, and answer judge. Sherpa DP trains on the four ID archetypes (None, Attempt, Subgoal, and Contrast); Sherpa NP trains on a single student archetype without a teaching strategy requirement (None). We also use a single student with other ID archetypes to train teachers and report their results in Appendix C.2.1 .
blocks.zh:
我们使用第3.1节所述的MATH过滤程序所保留的759个培训和528个评价问题。
在训练期间,我们为Qune3-8B师生和Qune3-1.7B师生禁用思维,并使用Qune3-8B作为指导门,适应门,答题法官的LLM裁判. Sherpa DP列车在四种ID型(无,尝试,次级目标,和对比); Sherpa NP列车在单一学生型上没有教学战略要求(无). 我们还利用一名学生和其他身份识别型号培训教师,并在附录C.2.1中报告结果。

blocks.en:
We implement training on AReaL ( Fu et al., 2025 ) , overlapping rollout generation with policy optimization, with up to 64 concurrent rollout tasks, a consumer batch size of 16, and a maximum policy-version lag of two.
The teacher uses rank-16 LoRA adapters with scaling parameter 16 on all linear projections. Each training step draws 16 problems and samples eight trajectories per problem. We train for 1500 updates using Adam with a learning rate of 5 × 10 − 5 5\times 10^{-5} , coefficients ( 0.9 , 0.999 ) (0.9,0.999) , epsilon 10 − 8 10^{-8} , no weight decay, gradient clipping at 1.0 1.0 , and a linear learning-rate warmup over one epoch, followed by a constant learning rate. We use a turn-level leave-one-out group baseline, a policy clipping threshold of 0.2, and no KL penalty. The student-improvement reward is assigned only to valid turns that pass both gates. Malformed outputs and exact repeated teacher responses receive a separate format or repetition penalty of − 0.5 -0.5 .

blocks.en: During training, the teacher has up to three preparation attempts, each capped at 4096 4096 tokens. A verified correct solution is kept private to the teacher and shared across trajectories for the same problem; a problem is skipped if no attempt succeeds. Tutoring permits at most 10 10 turns, and the teacher may end earlier. During testing, we sample 8 8 unaided and 8 8 post-tutoring samples on the original problem to estimate the student’s improvement. Teacher sampling uses temperature 1.0 and top- p p 1.0, with a cap of 1024 1024 tokens per tutoring response. The training prompts and response format are provided in Appendix D.2 .

Since untrained Qwen3-8B struggles to follow the required format in long contexts, we remove the private-reasoning format requirement and let it output the response directly. Appendix D.3 specifies the response templates and answer judge.

blocks.en: We implement the PedagogicalRL baseline on the AReaL infrastructure following its official method, which combines student success with leakage and helpfulness judgments. The baseline uses the same Qwen3-8B backbone, rank-16 LoRA adapters, and 1500 training updates. Its frozen configuration uses eight sampled trajectories per group, a 5 × 10 − 5 5\times 10^{-5} learning rate, a warmup proportion of 0.001 0.001 , and a 1024 1024 -token response cap. Its evaluation uses the same student archetypes and the held-out judge as our teachers do. We align its required output format with ours so that subsequent comparisons are not affected by differences in format requirements.

blocks.en: We compute 95% percentile confidence intervals using 10000 question-level bootstrap resamples. Each resample draws 528 problems with replacement, retaining all seven student archetypes and their eight test outcomes per problem, together with the corresponding unaided baselines. The same sampled problem indices are used across teachers for paired comparisons. These intervals quantify question-sampling uncertainty.
blocks.zh: 我们用一万个问题级的靴子来计算95%的置信间隔。 每一次再试抽取了528个与替换有关的问题,保留了所有7个学生型号及其每个问题的8个测试结果,以及相应的无辅助基线. 教师之间采用同样的抽样问题指数进行对等比较。 这些间隔量化了问题抽样不确定性。

blocks.en: B.3 MathTutorBench Evaluation Details
blocks.zh: B.3 数学图器 法官评审详情

blocks.en: Problem Solving and Mistake Correction are measured by accuracy, Socratic Questioning by BLEU against reference questions, Solution Correctness by F1 for classifying student solutions as correct or incorrect, and Mistake Location by micro-F1 for identifying the first incorrect step. The four teacher response generation tasks use Ped-RM win rates: the proportion of model responses preferred over reference human-teacher responses by the benchmark’s pedagogical reward model. Pedagogy Average is the mean of these four win rates.
blocks.zh: 问题解决和错误校正用精度测量,由BLEU针对参考问题进行 Socratic 质询,由F1对学生解决方案分类为正确或不正确,由Micro-F1对错误校正定位用于识别第一个错误步骤. 四个师资反应生成任务使用Ped-RM取胜率:基准教学奖励模式比参考人师反应优先的模型反应比例. 教学法 平均是这四个胜率的平均值.

blocks.en: We retain the benchmark task prompts and apply the following response-processing rules. Because the original benchmark stopping rules can unnecessarily truncate evaluated responses at paragraph breaks or task headings, we keep only the line-start Teacher and Student labels as stopping boundaries and remove the other stopping rules. For Solution Correctness, we use the final explicit Yes/No judgment rather than the first, since the model may provide its answer after reasoning.
blocks.zh: 我们保留基准任务提示并适用以下反应处理规则。 因为原始的基准停止规则可以在段落断开或任务标题上不必要地截取被评价的响应,所以我们只保留线起站点的"师生"标签作为停止边界并去掉其他停止规则. 对于解决方案正确性,我们使用最后明确的是/否判断而不是第一个判断,因为模型可能在推理后提供答案。

blocks.en: Following the benchmark’s default decoding settings, Qwen models use temperature 0 0 and a 2048 2048 -token output cap, with thinking disabled. Gemini uses medium reasoning with temperature 1.0 1.0 .
blocks.zh: 根据基准默认的解码设置,Quen模型使用温度0和2048 2048 - token输出盖,思维被禁用. 双子座使用中等推理,温度为1.01.0.

blocks.en: B.4 Human Study Details
blocks.zh: B.4 人类研究细节

blocks.en: We use 80 CoMTA dialogue contexts labeled Answer Not Accepted . For each context, Gemini generates one short student request for each of four instructional needs: Subgoal, Contrast, Causal, and Error Anticipation. The generated request is appended to the student’s original wording. The prompt for generating these requests is provided in Appendix D.4 . Subgoal and Contrast correspond to training preferences, while Causal and Error Anticipation are unseen instructional needs. Because not all preferences can be naturally appended to the student’s response, we introduce Error Anticipation as a new held-out preference.
blocks.zh: 我们使用80 COMTA 对话框, 对于每一种情况,双子座因四个教学需求,即次级目标、对比、因果和错误预测,而产生一个短期学生申请。 由学生提出的申请附在学生的原文后。 发出这些请求的时机见附录D.4。 次级目标和对照对应的培训偏好,而Causal和Error Expectiation则是看不见的教学需要。 因为并非所有的偏好都可以自然地附在学生的回应中,所以我们引入了“错失预期”作为新的搁置偏好。

blocks.en:
We compare Sherpa DP with the untrained Qwen3-8B backbone. Both receive the same tutoring prompt, which requests a short response and asks the teacher to check and, where necessary, correct the student’s last message. Generation uses temperature 0.7 0.7 , top- p p 0.8 0.8 , top- k k 20 20 , a 2048 2048 -token cap, and disabled thinking. Only the student-facing output is displayed, with private reasoning removed and mathematical notation converted to readable plain text.
Model identities are hidden, and order is randomized during comparison. The generation and annotation prompts are in Appendix D.4 .
blocks.zh:
我们比较了Sherpa DP和未经训练的 Quen3 -8B 骨干。 两者都收到同样的辅导提示,要求简短的答复,并要求教师检查并在必要时纠正学生的最后信息。 一代使用温度0.7 0.7,顶端-p 0.8 0.8,顶端-k k 20 20,一个2048 2048 -token cap, 和残疾思维. 仅显示学生相遇的输出,删除了私人推理并转换为可读的平正文字.
模型身份被隐藏,在比较时顺序被随机化. 生成和注释提示载于附录D.4。

blocks.en: The full study recruited 96 high school teachers with at least a bachelor’s degree and English proficiency via Prolific. Each teacher evaluated ten items, with three judgments per item, for 960 judgments. Participants read the conversation and both responses, selected “ Response A ”, “ Response B ”, or “ About the same ”, and optionally provided a brief explanation. Instructions ask them to compare teaching quality and not judge by length, formatting, or other surface features alone. Compensation rate was $16 per hour. The final dataset contains three judgments for every item.
blocks.zh: 全面研究通过Prolific招聘了96名至少具有学士学位和英语熟练程度的高中教师。 每个教师对960项判决进行了10项评价,每项判决3项。 与会者阅读了谈话和两个答复,选定了“答复A”、“答复B”或“大约相同”,并可选择作出简要说明。 指令要求他们比较教学质量,而不是仅仅通过长度,格式或其他表面特征来判断. 补偿率为每小时16美元。 最终数据集包含每个项目的三个判断.

blocks.en: B.5 Student Simulator Analysis Settings
blocks.zh: B.5 学生模拟分析设置

blocks.en:
We sample 50 problems without replacement from the 528-problem evaluation set to conduct the analysis. The teacher is GPT-5.6-Luna with medium reasoning, with instruction to teach using one assigned strategy throughout the dialogue (the prompts are provided in Appendix D.5 ).
Other evaluation setting is the same as default.
blocks.zh:
我们从528个问题评价组中抽取50个问题,但没有进行替换,以进行分析。 教师是GPT-5.6-Luna,具有中等推理能力,在整个对话期间,教他使用一种指定战略授课(附录D.5提供了提示)。
其他评价设置与默认相同.

blocks.en:
For our student archetypes, when the gate rejects a message, we randomly select one of six fixed responses that only express the student’s lack of understanding, avoiding the influence of explanations of the rejection on teaching.
The prompted variant disables external adaptive gating and instead appends the same preference criterion to each student request.
It asks the student to assess the teacher’s latest message internally, work on the mathematics if the criterion is met, and otherwise return only a specified complaint from the same pool.
blocks.zh:
对于我们的学生,当大门拒绝一个信息时,我们随机选择六个只表示学生缺乏理解的固定响应中的一个,避免了拒绝的解释对教学的影响.
被激发的变体会禁用外部的适应取景,而是将相同的偏好标准附加到每个学生的请求上.
它要求学生在内部评估老师的最新信息,如果符合标准则进行数学研究,否则只从同一个人才库中返回一个具体的投诉.

blocks.en: B.6 Training-objective Comparison Settings
blocks.zh: B.6 培训-目标比较设置

blocks.en: We compare the base Qwen3-8B model, Sherpa DP , and two gate-penalty variants with penalty magnitudes of 0.25 and 0.5. Both variants use the same training setup as Sherpa DP . In each variant, we apply penalties for gate violations, with a magnitude of 0.25 or 0.5 depending on the variant.
blocks.zh: 我们比较了基座的Qwen3-8B模型Sherpa DP,以及两个门-惩罚变体,其罚分为0.25和0.5. 两个变体都使用与Sherpa DP相同的训练设置. 在每个变体中,我们适用对入门违规的处罚,根据变体的不同,处罚幅度为0.25或0.5.

blocks.en: Appendix C Additional Results and Analyses
blocks.zh: 附录C 成果和分析

blocks.en: C.1 Effect of Preparation
blocks.zh: C.1 准备的效果

blocks.en: Table 4: Student test accuracy after teaching (%) by Qwen3-8B with and without preparation. Overall 95% confidence intervals use the same question-level bootstrap procedure as the main table.
blocks.zh: 表4:有准备和无准备的Quen3-8B在教学后的学生测试精度(%)。 总体而言,95%的置信间隔使用与主表相同的问题级拖带程序。

blocks.en:
To examine the effect of preparation on teaching performance, we evaluate Qwen3-8B with and without preparation, using the default evaluation setting.
In Table 4 , preparation raises overall accuracy from 45.3% to 48.6%, a gain of 3.3 percentage points. ID accuracy increases from 44.9% to 49.1%, while OOD accuracy increases from 45.9% to 47.9%.
These results support the use of preparation in the main evaluation, while showing that its benefit is not uniform across preferences.
blocks.zh:
为了审查准备对教学表现的影响,我们利用默认的评价设置,对Qune3-8B进行有准备和无准备的评价。
在表4中,编制将总体准确度从45.3%提高到48.6%,增幅为3.3个百分点。 ID精度由44.9%提高到49.1%,而OD精度由45.9%提高到47.9%.
这些结果支持在主要评价中采用准备工作,同时表明其好处在各种偏好之间并不一致。

blocks.en: C.2 Additional Evaluation on Student Archetypes
blocks.zh: C.2 对学生考古类型的补充评价

blocks.en: C.2.1 Training on Individual Archetypes
blocks.zh: C.2.1 个别考古类型的培训

blocks.en:
To ablate the student archetypes used for training, we compare teachers trained on individual archetypes with the teacher trained on all ID archetypes.
We include teachers trained with a single student with Attempt, Subgoal, and Contrast as preferences in Table 5 , using the same training and evaluation setting as Sherpa DP .
We additionally include Gemini 3.8 Flash as a strong external general-purpose model in the complete results below. It is reported separately from the Qwen3-8B models and excluded from the bold highlighting.
blocks.zh:
为了减少用于培训的学生的型号,我们把接受过个别型号培训的教师与接受过所有ID型号培训的教师进行比较。
在表5中,我们用与Sherpa DP相同的培训和评价环境,将接受过单独培训的具有尝试、次级目标和对比性的学生作为偏好。
我们还将双子座 3.8 Flash作为强有力的外部通用模型列入下文的全部结果。 它与Qwen3-8B模型分开报告,被排除在粗体突出显示之外.

blocks.en: Table 5: Complete student-archetype results, including all single-archetype teachers and Gemini 3.8 Flash as an external reference. Values are student test accuracy after teaching (%). Bold values indicate the best result in each column among models sharing the Qwen3-8B backbone.
blocks.zh: 表5:完整学生-Archetype结果,包括所有单Archetype教师和双子座 3.8 Flash作为外部参考. 数值是教学后的学生测试精度(%). 粗体值表示每个列在共享Qune3-8B主干线的模型中的最佳结果.

blocks.en:
Table 5 shows that training the Qwen3-8B base model with Sherpa enables Sherpa DP to achieve overall student test accuracy comparable to Gemini 3.8 Flash (69.0% versus 70.1%), and each single-archetype teacher exceeds Sherpa NP ’s overall accuracy of 52.0%. However, training on a preference does not consistently yield the best performance on that same preference. Among the Qwen3-8B teachers, Subgoal has the highest ID average, at 74.5%, while Sherpa DP achieves the highest OOD and overall averages, at 65.1% and 69.0%, respectively. Although the Subgoal-trained teacher also performs well, we argue that this is because the Subgoal preference itself is particularly helpful to the student model.
Table 6 further demonstrate that training on all ID archetypes yields the strongest overall teaching performance and generalization on MathTutorBench.
blocks.zh:
表5显示,用Sherpa培训Qune3-8B基模使Sherpa DP能够实现与双子座3.8 Flash(69.0%对70.1%)相仿的学生测试总精度,每个单管型教师都超过了Sherpa NP52.0%的总精度. 但是,关于优惠的培训不能始终以同样的优惠取得最佳业绩。 在Quen3-8B教师中,次级目标的平均身份证最高,为74.5%,而Shelpa DP的平均水平最高,分别为65.1%和69.0%。 虽然接受次级目标培训的教师也表现良好,但我们认为这是因为次级目标偏好本身对学生模式特别有帮助。
表6还表明,关于所有ID型型的培训,在MathTutor Bench上的总体教学表现和概括性最强。

blocks.en: Table 6: Complete MathTutorBench scores (%), including all single-archetype teachers and Gemini 3.8 Flash as an external reference. Bold values indicate the best result in each column among models sharing the Qwen3-8B backbone.
blocks.zh: 表6: MathTutor Bench的完整分数 (%),包括所有单管型教师和双子座 3.8 Flash作为外部参考. 粗体值表示每个列在共享Qune3-8B主干线的模型中的最佳结果.

blocks.en: Different single-archetype teachers exhibit different strengths. While their performance on math expertise and student understanding is broadly comparable, Sherpa DP outperforms all single-archetype teachers on every teacher response generation metric. This demonstrates the improved generalization and teaching capabilities obtained by training with diverse students. As a strong general-purpose model, Gemini scores markedly higher on MathTutorBench’s mathematical problem-solving and diagnosis tasks. However, Sherpa DP achieves a higher Pedagogy Average (79.2% versus 72.4%) and higher scores on the benchmark’s standard and hard instruction-following tasks. Although our base model scores lower than Gemini on mathematical problem solving, training raises its instruction-following win rate from 74.0% to 90.3%, exceeding Gemini’s 69.9%, with gains also extending to the hard setting and its overall Pedagogy Average increasing from 52.5% to 79.2%. This echoes our initial motivation: stronger problem-solving ability does not automatically translate into better teaching.
blocks.zh: 不同的单体型教师表现出不同的长处. 虽然他们在数学专业知识和学生理解方面的表现大致可以比较,但Shelpa DP在每一个教师响应生成度量标准上都超过了所有单型教师. 这表明,通过对不同学生的培训,普遍化和教学能力得到了提高。 作为强大的通用模型,双子座在MathTutor Bench的数学问题解析和诊断任务上的得分明显更高. 然而,Shelpa DP实现了更高的平均教学率(79.2%比72.4%)和更高的基准标准教学和硬性教学任务的分数。 尽管我们的基础模型在数学问题解答上得分低于双子座,但培训将跟随教学的胜率从74.0%提高到90.3%,超过了双子座69.9%,收益也延伸到了硬地环境,整体教学平均率从52.5%提高到79.2%。 这与我们最初的动机相呼应:更强的解决问题的能力不会自动转化为更好的教学。

blocks.en: C.2.2 Further Analysis of Teaching Gains
blocks.zh: C.2.2 进一步分析教学成果

blocks.en: We examine each teacher’s improvement from two perspectives: how often its messages satisfy student preferences and pass the gates, and the teaching quality of those accepted messages.
blocks.zh: 我们从两个角度审视每个教师的改进情况:其信息如何满足学生的喜好并传递大门,以及这些被接受信息的教学质量。

blocks.en: Satisfying Student Preferences. We consider a message to satisfy student preferences when it is valid and passes both the guidance and adaptive gates. For each trajectory, we compute the fraction of teacher messages for interaction that satisfy these conditions and reach the student. Since trajectories differ in dialogue length, we average these fractions across trajectories with equal weights.
blocks.zh: 满足学生偏好. 我们认为,当信息是有效的并经过指导和适应性的大门时,就满足学生的偏好。 对于每个轨迹,我们计算出教师信息中满足这些条件并到达学生的交互部分. 由于相对话长度的轨距不同,所以我们平均以等重的轨距取出这些分数.

blocks.en: Table 7: Student preference satisfaction rates (%).
blocks.zh: 表7:学生喜好满意率(%)。

blocks.en: Teaching Quality. We examine accepted teaching from two angles: how much a single round helps the student and how many rounds the teacher delivers.
blocks.zh: 教学质量. 我们从两个角度来研究被接受的教学:一回合对学生帮助多少,以及老师提供多少回合.

blocks.en: Single-round effect. We rerun the evaluation, stopping each dialogue immediately after the first accepted teacher message and the student’s reply. We report student improvement on trajectories with an accepted message, so that each evaluated student receives exactly one round of teaching.
blocks.zh: 单圆相克. 我们重新进行评估, 我们用一个可接受的信息来报告学生的轨迹改善情况,这样,每个被评价的学生都能得到准确的一轮教学。

blocks.en: Table 8: Student improvement after one accepted teaching round (pp).
blocks.zh: 表8:在接受一轮教学后学生的提高(下册)。

blocks.en: Amount of teaching. In the full evaluation, we count the accepted teacher messages per trajectory and report the average number of effective teaching turns received by the student.
blocks.zh: 教学量. 在全面评价中,我们计算每个轨迹中接受的教师信息,并报告学生得到的有效教学转折的平均数量。

blocks.en: Table 9: Average number of effective teaching turns.
blocks.zh: 表9:有效教学转折的平均次数。

blocks.en: Analysis. Table 10 summarizes these measurements alongside overall student improvement, averaged across the seven student archetypes.
blocks.zh: 分析。 表10汇总了这些衡量结果,以及学生总体改善情况,这平均涉及7个学生类型。

blocks.en: Table 10: Preference satisfaction, teaching quality, and overall student improvement.
blocks.zh: 表10:优先程度、教学质量和学生整体改善情况。

blocks.en: Sherpa DP combines the highest preference satisfaction rate with strong single-round teaching, while maintaining a moderate number of effective turns. Compared with the base model and Sherpa NP , it achieves greater overall improvement with fewer accepted turns, suggesting more efficient teaching. It also delivers more effective turns than Subgoal and Contrast while retaining a comparable single-round effect. Contrast illustrates why strong individual replies alone may be insufficient: despite having the highest single-round improvement and a preference satisfaction rate close to Attempt’s, it delivers only 1.0 effective turns per trajectory, compared with Attempt’s 1.7, and achieves lower overall improvement. These results suggest that teaching gains depend jointly on satisfying student preferences, delivering useful instruction, and sustaining the interaction.
blocks.zh: Sherpa DP将最高的喜好满意率与强力的单轮教学相结合,同时保持了适度的有效转会. 与基础模型和Shelpa NP相比,它以更少的被接受的转弯实现更大的整体改进,表明教学效率更高. 它还提供比次级目标和对照更有效的转会,同时保持类似的单一回合效果。 与此相矛盾的是,单靠个人的有力答复可能是不够的:尽管单回合改进率最高,而且优惠满意率接近尝试,但与尝试1.7相比,每个轨迹只提供1.0个有效转弯,总体改善率较低。 这些结果表明,教学成果共同取决于学生的喜好、提供有用的教学和维持互动。

blocks.en: C.2.3 Generalization to Unseen Student Backbones
blocks.zh: C.2.3 向不明学生后骨进行通缩

blocks.en:
To examine transfer across student model families, we evaluate the teacher checkpoints used with Gemma-3-1B-IT ( Team et al., 2025 ) and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct ( Grattafiori et al., 2024 ) as students.
Table 11 shows that Sherpa DP achieves the highest accuracy for every archetype with both student backbones. Overall accuracy rises from 14.3% to 21.7% with Gemma and from 37.5% to 53.5% with Llama, compared with the untrained teacher. These gains indicate that the learned teaching behavior transfers beyond the Qwen3-1.7B student used during training.
More interestingly, although PedagogicalRL and Sherpa NP improve over the base model in Table 1 , they provide little or no improvement over the base model when evaluated with other student models, indicating weaker generalization.This further highlights that training with diverse student archetypes generalizes not only to unseen preferences but also to other student models.
blocks.zh:
为了检查跨学生模范家庭的转学情况,我们评价与Gemma-3-1B-IT(Team等,2025年)和Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct(Grattafiori等,2024年)一起使用的教师检查站为学生。
表11显示,Sherpa DP对每个有两种学生骨干的主干型都达到了最高的准确度. 与未受过培训的教师相比,Gemma的总精度从14.3%上升到21.7%,Llama的总精度从37.5%上升到53.5%. 这些成绩表明,学到的教学行为转移超越了训练期间使用的Quen3-1.7B学生.
更有趣的是,虽然"教学RL"和"Shelpa NP"在表1中的基础模型上有所改进,但在与其他学生模型评价时,它们提供的比基础模型的改进很少或根本没有,这表明概括性较弱. 这进一步突出表明,具有不同学生类型的培训不仅概括为无形的偏好,而且还概括为其他学生模式。

blocks.en: Table 11: Student test accuracy after teaching (%) with alternative student backbones. Bold values mark the best teacher for each student backbone. Overall 95% confidence intervals use 10000 bootstrap resamples of problems.
blocks.zh: 表11: 具有替代学生骨干教学后的学生测试精度(%). 粗体的价值观是每个学生骨干的最佳教师。 总体而言,95%的置信间隔使用10 000个靴子的后遗症。

blocks.en: C.2.4 Multiple Training Run
blocks.zh: C.2.4 多重训练

blocks.en:
Table 12 compares three independent training runs of our standard model using different random seeds, with the same training setup.
We use the first one to report in Table 1 .
Across the three seeds, mean overall accuracy is 68.9 ± 2.0 % 68.9\pm 2.0\% , with ID and OOD accuracies of 72.2 ± 1.6 % 72.2\pm 1.6\% and 64.4 ± 2.6 % 64.4\pm 2.6\% , respectively, where ± \pm denotes the sample standard deviation across training seeds.
Table 12: Student test accuracy after teaching (%) across three training seeds. Mean and SD summarize the three training runs; SD is the sample standard deviation across training seeds.
blocks.zh: 表12:三个培训种子教学后学生测试精度(%)。 平均和自毁总结了三次训练;自毁是训练种子的样本标准偏差。

blocks.en: C.2.5 Transfer Across Teacher Model Families
blocks.zh: C.2.5 跨教师模范家庭调动

blocks.en:
To examine whether our framework transfers across teacher model families, we train a Ministral-3-8B-Instruct ( Liu et al., 2026 ) teacher on all four ID archetypes for 300 updates and compare it with its untrained backbone.
Training with Sherpa improves student accuracy across all seven archetypes. Overall accuracy increases from 39.6% to 55.0%, with ID accuracy increasing from 39.5% to 59.4% and OOD accuracy from 39.8% to 49.2%.
blocks.zh:
为了检查我们的框架是否跨越教师模范家庭,我们培训了一名Ministry-3-8B-Instruct(Liu等,2026年)教师,学习所有四种ID型型,更新300种,并与未经培训的骨干进行比较。
与Sherpa进行的培训提高了所有7个典型类型学生的准确性。 总精度由39.6%提高到55.0%,ID精度由39.5%提高到59.4%,OO精度由39.8%提高到49.2%.

blocks.en:
We test whether different student model families, used without adaptive gates, already prefer different teaching strategies.
Each of Qwen3-1.7B, Gemma-3-1B-IT, and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is paired with the six fixed strategies from Section 3.4 .
Figure 5 shows large differences in how much each model improves: Gemma gains much less than the other two, reflecting differences in learning ability.
However, the pattern across strategies is similar for all three.
Changing the model family therefore does not change which strategies it responds to.

我们测试不同的学生模范家庭,在没有适应性门的情况下使用,是否已经倾向于不同的教学策略.

blocks.en:
Section 3.4 also finds that prompted students give less informative feedback than our gated archetypes.
On replies from mismatched strategy-preference pairs, we report two rates for eligible nonempty replies in Table 14 . Contains complaint counts replies in which the prescribed complaint phrase appears; correct complaint counts replies that match that complaint exactly after normalization.
For our design, the two rates are identical by design, because a rejected instruction is replaced by the scripted complaint alone.
Prompted students include a complaint at a similar rate (65.3% versus 76.9%), but return a complaint-only reply only 28.9% of the time.
The complaint is usually embedded in a continued solution, so the student keeps working on the problem even when the instruction misses the assigned preference.

第3.4节还发现,促使学生提供的反馈信息少于我们的门类。

对于我们的设计来说,这两种费率在设计上是相同的,因为一个被拒绝的指令被只被脚本上的投诉所取而代之.
被录取的学生包括同样比例的投诉(65.3%对76.9%),但只回复28.9%的投诉。
投诉通常被嵌入到持续解决方案中,因此即使教学错过了指定的偏好,学生也会继续研究这个问题.

blocks.en: C.4 Analysis of Different Training Designs
blocks.zh: C.4 不同培训设计的分析

blocks.en:
Table 15 reports per-archetype accuracy for the training-objective comparison in the main paper.
A gate penalty of 0.25 slightly raises ID accuracy (72.7% versus 72.0% for Sherpa DP ) and slightly lowers OOD accuracy (64.2% versus 65.1%), leaving overall accuracy essentially unchanged (69.1% versus 69.0%).
Increasing the penalty to 0.5 reduces ID, OOD, and overall accuracy to 61.7%, 51.8%, and 57.5%, respectively. On MathTutorBench, increasing the penalty from 0.25 to 0.5 also lowers all four pedagogical scores. Together, these results show that stronger gate penalties worsen teaching performance and generalization rather than improve them.

blocks.en: C.5 Effect of Turn-level Masking
blocks.zh: C.5 上下层面具的效果

blocks.en: Our training uses student improvement as the reward together with turn-level masking. A natural question is whether the gains mainly come from masking rather than the student-improvement signal. To examine this, we compare Sherpa DP with a variant using standard episode-level GRPO, which assigns the trajectory reward to every turn without masking and uses an episode-level leave-one-out baseline. The local format and repetition penalties remain unchanged. We compare all trained teachers after 500 updates, which already reveal substantial performance gains.
blocks.zh: 我们的训练把学生的改进作为奖励 加上转弯的口罩 一个自然的问题就是收益是否主要来自蒙面而不是学生改进信号. 为了检查这一点,我们用标准分集级GRPO来将Sherpa DP与一个变体进行比较,这个变体将轨迹奖励分配给每个转弯而不蒙上面具,并使用分集级放行一出的基准. 地方形式和重复处罚保持不变。 我们比较了经过500次更新后所有受过培训的教师,这些更新已经显示出显著的成绩。

blocks.en: Table 16 shows that even within 500 updates, training without masking achieves 58.6% overall student accuracy, close to the 59.5% achieved with masking. Both already outperform Sherpa NP (51.8%), PedagogicalRL (51.5%), and the untrained backbone (48.6%). These results support student improvement as an effective training signal: substantial gains emerge with or without turn-level masking.
blocks.zh: 表16显示,即使更新了500种,没有蒙面的培训也达到了学生整体准确度的58.6%,接近有蒙面效果的59.5%。 两者都已经超过了Sherpa NP(51.8%)、教育RL(51.5%)和未经培训的骨干(48.6%)。 这些结果支持学生的提高,作为一种有效的培训信号:无论有无转弯层的遮掩,都会产生实质性成果。

blocks.en: Then the reason for us to use masking is to concentrate the student-improvement signal on valid, gate-accepted turns, which encourages more efficient teaching behavior with higher gate acceptance and shorter dialogues. Over the first 500 updates, training with masking averages 5.0 turns per episode, compared with 8.1 without masking, and generates approximately 161k tokens per update instead of 260k. Across 500 updates, this amounts to approximately 80.5 million versus 130 million tokens. Masking thus achieves comparable performance with shorter dialogues and approximately 38% fewer generated training tokens.
blocks.zh: 然后我们使用口罩的理由是把学生改进的信号集中在有效的,被门接受的转弯上,这鼓励了更高的门接受率和更短的对话率来提高教学行为的效率. 在前500个更新中,每集平均有5.0个口罩的训练,而8.1个没有口罩的口罩,每集更新产生约161k个令牌,而不是260k. 在500个更新中,这一数字约为8 050万个,而1亿3千万个。 因此,通过缩短对话,蒙面效果可以比较好,而生成的培训符号大约会减少38%。

blocks.en: D.1.1 Guidance Gate Prompt

blocks.en: The guidance gate checks whether the teacher message contains the reference answer, either directly or as a numerical expression that evaluates to it. The following system message and user template are used together; the gate rejects a message when the returned leaked field is true . Template variables are filled with the reference answer and the student-visible teacher message.
blocks.zh: 指导门检查教师信息是否包含参考答案,要么是直接的,要么是作为对它进行评价的数字表达. 下面的系统消息和用户模板一起使用;当返回的被泄露的字段是真实的时,闸门拒绝消息. 模板变量由参考答案和学生可见的教师信息填充.

blocks.en: Guidance gate System message Mechanically judge answer containment. Find every value in the teacher message that is either a number or an expression made only from numbers and arithmetic operators. Convert LaTeX arithmetic notation, compute those values exactly, and normalize them with the ground truth. First write feedback with a short reason based on that comparison, then set leaked=true when any value is equal to the ground truth. Return valid JSON only with keys feedback (string) and leaked (boolean), in that order. User message template Ground Truth: {{ ground_truth }} Teacher Message: {{ teacher_action or ’(empty)’ }} After extracting and computing numeric content from the teacher message, does any extracted value equal the ground truth? Return JSON only with this schema: { "feedback": "<short explanation>", "leaked": <boolean> }
blocks.zh: 指导门系统信息 机械判断员回答封装。 在师资信件中查找仅从数字和算术操作器中生成的数字或表达式的每个值。 转换LaTeX的算术符号,准确计算这些值,使其与地表真理正常化. 首先根据这种比较写出简短的反馈,然后当任何值等于地面真理时设置出漏出=真. 返回有效的 JSON 只使用密钥反馈( 字符串) 和漏出( 布尔), 按此顺序 。 用户消息模板 地面真相 : __地_真相__. 教师信息: \ 老师_ 行动 或 (空) \ \ \ \ 在从师资信息中提取和计算出数字内容后,是否有任何提取值等于地心真理? 返回 JSON 只使用这个方案 : { "feedback" : "<short explain>","leaked" : <boolean > }

blocks.en: D.1.2 Adaptive Gate Prompts

blocks.en: All six adaptive gates share the system message and user template below. The preference variable is replaced by the corresponding archetype-specific text in the following blocks, in the order introduced in § 2.2 . The other variables contain the problem, the latest student message, and the current teacher message. When no previous student message exists, last_student_message is set to “No previous real student message is available.”

blocks.en: Adaptive gates: shared prompt System message You judge whether a tutor message follows one stated student preference. Judge the teaching approach, not mathematical correctness. Ignore tone, politeness, and verbosity. If the preference requires a previous student response but no previous real student message is available, return PASS so the student can respond first. Reply with exactly these two XML elements, with the reasoning before the verdict: <reasoning>brief reason</reasoning> <verdict>PASS</verdict> Set verdict to PASS exactly when the tutor message satisfies the preference; otherwise set it to FAIL. Ensure the verdict agrees with the reasoning. Use only PASS or FAIL inside the verdict element. Put nothing outside the two elements. blocks.en: Attempt diagnosis The student wants feedback on their latest attempt. PASS if the tutor identifies a specific part of that attempt as correct, incorrect, or missing and explains why. FAIL if the tutor gives only a general judgment or moves on without addressing the attempt.
blocks.zh: 尝试诊断 学生希望得到他们最新尝试的反馈. 如果辅导员确定这一尝试的特定部分是正确、不正确或缺失的,并解释原因。 如果导师只给出一般的判断,或者在不考虑尝试的情况下继续前进,则会发现错误。

blocks.en: Causal justification The student wants to understand why a specific mathematical claim or step holds. PASS if the tutor directly explains why it follows by applying a relevant mathematical rule, definition, or relationship. FAIL if the tutor only states the claim, describes how to proceed, or leaves the reason implicit.
blocks.zh: 因果关系 学生想了解一个特定的数学主张或步骤为何存在. 如果导师通过应用相关的数学规则、定义或关系来直接解释其遵循的原因,则PASS. FAIL 如果导师只陈述要求,描述如何进行,或者隐含原因.

blocks.en: Subgoal decomposition The student wants the problem organized around subgoals. PASS if the tutor states the current subgoal and explains how it helps reach the overall goal. FAIL if the tutor gives only a flat list of steps, states only the next operation, or solves without exposing the structure.
blocks.zh: 次级目标分解 学生希望这个问题围绕次级目标来组织. 如果辅导员说明目前的次级目标,并解释如何帮助实现总体目标。 FAIL 如果导师只给出一个平整的步数列表,只表示下个操作,或者解开而不暴露结构.

blocks.en: Step demonstration The student wants to watch the tutor perform one step on the current problem. PASS if the tutor carries out exactly one new step, shows the resulting intermediate state, briefly explains it, and then stops. FAIL if the tutor only describes the step, uses another example, performs multiple steps, or gives the final answer.
blocks.zh: 步骤演示 学生想看导师在目前问题上表演一步. PASS 如果导师完全执行一个新的步骤, 显示结果的中间状态, 简单解释一下, 然后停止。 FAIL 如果导师只描述步骤,使用另一个示例,执行多个步骤,或者给出最后的答案.

blocks.en: Independent verification The student wants a previous mathematical result checked independently. PASS immediately if no previous real student message is available. Otherwise, an independent check must either derive the same result from the original problem by a different method, or test the claimed result directly against the original conditions. PASS only if the tutor completes that check and states whether it confirms or refutes the result. FAIL if the tutor only evaluates, corrects, or reuses the student’s working, continues toward a new result, or asks the student to finish the check.
blocks.zh: 独立核查 学生想要独立检查之前的数学结果 。 如果之前没有真正的学生信息,则立即提供PASS。 否则,独立检查要么必须用不同的方法从最初的问题中得出相同的结果,要么直接根据原始条件检验声称的结果。 PASS 只有当导师完成检查并声明它是否确认或反驳了结果时。 如果导师只评价、纠正或重复学生的工作,继续取得新的结果,或要求学生完成检查,则FAIL。

blocks.en: Contrastive comparison The student wants two plausible local alternatives compared directly. PASS if the tutor presents two alternatives for the same decision and explains the key mathematical difference between them. FAIL if only one alternative is shown, the alternatives are unrelated, or their decisive difference is not explained.
blocks.zh: 对比比较 学生直接想要两种可行的本地选择。 如果导师为同一决定提出两种选择,并解释它们之间的关键数学差异。 如果仅显示一个替代品,则该替代品无关,或未解释其决定性差异。

blocks.en: D.1.3 Adaptive-gate Feedback
blocks.zh: D.1.3 适应门反馈

blocks.en: The training run and main student-archetype evaluation use the following preference-specific feedback pool when an adaptive gate rejects a teacher response. The bare complaint pool used in the simulator analysis is listed in Appendix D.5 .
blocks.zh: 训练运行和主要的学生-Archetype评价在适应性门拒绝教师回应时使用以下针对偏好性的反馈池. 模拟分析中使用的赤裸的投诉池列于附录D.5.

blocks.en: Attempt diagnosis feedback Please stay with my last attempt: point out the specific part that is right, wrong, or missing, and tell me why. Please respond to the work I just showed: identify one specific correct or incorrect step and explain your assessment. Do not start a new solution yet; check my latest attempt, locate the first gap or mistake, and tell me why it is a problem. Could you examine my reasoning itself and say exactly which part holds and which part needs correction? Use my last response as the starting point: diagnose a concrete misconception or omission and explain it. I need targeted feedback on my attempt, not a general lesson; point to the exact line or idea that should stay or change and explain why.
blocks.zh: 尝试诊断反馈 请保持我的最后一次尝试:指出具体部分是正确,错误,还是缺失,告诉我原因. 请回答我刚才显示的工作:确定一个具体正确或不正确的步骤并解释你的评估。 不要启动新的解决方案; 请检查我最近的尝试, 找到第一个漏洞或错误, 告诉我为什么这是一个问题 。 你能看看我的推理本身,并说出究竟哪一部分是属于哪个部分,哪个部分需要更正? 用我最后的答复作为起点:诊断一个具体的误解或遗漏,并解释它。 我需要有针对性地反馈我的努力,而不是一般性的教训;指出应该留下或改变的确切路线或想法,并解释原因。

blocks.en: Causal justification feedback Before we continue, explain why this step or claim is valid instead of just naming the rule. Please explain the reason this claim follows from the relevant rule rather than only telling me what to do next. I need the why here: connect the definition or principle to the step we are using. Do not just state the formula; show why it applies to this particular step. Could you justify the current step by explaining the mathematical relationship that makes it valid? Before another calculation, explain what makes this inference true and how the rule leads to it.
blocks.zh: 原因说明反馈 在我们继续之前,解释为什么这个步骤或主张是有效的,而不是仅仅点出规则的名来. 请解释这一说法来自有关规则的原因,而不是仅仅告诉我下一步要做什么。 我需要这里的原因:将定义或原则与我们正在采取的步骤联系起来。 不要仅仅说明公式;说明它为什么适用于这一特定步骤。 您能否通过解释使其有效的数学关系来证明当前步骤的合理性 ? 在另一种计算之前,解释是什么使得这个推论是真实的,以及规则如何导致它.

blocks.en: Subgoal decomposition feedback I am losing the structure. Tell me our current subgoal and how it helps us reach the final goal. Please orient me: name the subgoal we are solving now and explain how its result moves us toward the whole problem. Break the remaining work into a current objective and the final objective, and tell me how they connect. I need the roadmap, not just the next operation: what intermediate goal are we pursuing, and why? Tell me which smaller goal we should complete at this point and what it unlocks afterward. Please organize this around subgoals by stating where we are now and how this part contributes to the final result.
blocks.zh: 次级目标分解反馈 我失去了结构。 告诉我我们目前的次级目标 以及它如何帮助我们实现最终目标 请指示我:说出我们现在正在解决的次级目标,并解释它的结果如何使我们走向整个问题。 将剩下的工作分解为当前的目标和最终目标,告诉我它们是如何联系在一起的. 我需要路线图,而不仅仅是下一个行动:我们追求的中间目标是什么,为什么? 告诉我我们现在应该完成 哪个小目标 以及它能解锁什么 请围绕次级目标来组织这项工作,说明我们现在在哪里,并说明这一部分如何为最终结果作出贡献。

blocks.en: Step demonstration feedback Please do one next step on this problem yourself, show me the result, briefly explain it, and then stop. Could you carry out only the next step on this exact problem, show the new intermediate expression, explain it briefly, and stop there? Please demonstrate one operation yourself on the current problem and leave the following step for me. I want to see one step, not a plan: perform it, show what the problem becomes, and then stop. Do exactly one new calculation or transformation here, explain why you chose it, and let me continue afterward. Please work one immediate step on these quantities, display the resulting state, and do not proceed to the next step or final answer.
blocks.zh: 步骤演示反馈 请自己做下一步的这个问题, 告诉我结果, 简单解释一下,然后停止。 你能否就这个问题采取下一步行动, 显示新的中间表达式, 简单解释一下,然后停下来? 请自己展示一次关于当前问题的操作,然后留给我下一步骤. 我想看到一个步骤,而不是一个计划: 执行它,显示问题变成什么,然后停止。 在这里做一个完全新的计算或转换,解释你选择它的原因,然后让我继续。 请立即就这些数量采取一个步骤,显示结果状态,不要进入下一步或最后答案。

blocks.en: Independent verification feedback Before we continue, check the current claim in a different way and show me what the check says. Please verify the claim with a different method, such as substitution or an inverse operation, and state what the result confirms. Do not repeat the same derivation; test the current result independently and show whether it checks out. Could you check this conclusion from another direction and explain what that check establishes? Before moving on, use a separate calculation or boundary check to verify the specific claim we have reached. I need an independent check of the current result, not reassurance; show the check and its conclusion.
blocks.zh: 独立核查反馈 在继续之前,用不同的方式检查目前的索赔,并告诉我支票上写了什么. 请用替代或倒置操作等不同方法核实索赔,并说明结果证实什么。 不要重复相同的推导; 独立测试当前结果并显示是否检查出 。 请从另一个方向检查这个结论,并解释该检查确定了什么? 在继续前进之前,使用单独的计算或边界检查来核实我们已经达成的具体索赔要求. 我需要对目前的结果进行独立的检查,而不是保证;显示检查及其结论。

blocks.en: Contrastive comparison feedback Show me two plausible choices here and explain the key difference that makes one work and the other fail. Please put two plausible approaches to this same step side by side and identify the mathematical difference between them. Show one option that works and one tempting option that fails here, then explain the decisive distinction. Could you compare two possible choices for the current decision and explain why their outcomes differ? Do not present only the correct route; contrast it with a plausible alternative and say exactly where they diverge. Give me two local alternatives for this step and explain the property that selects one over the other.
blocks.zh: 对比比较反馈 给我看两个可行的选择 并解释关键的区别 使一个工作,另一个失败。 请将两种可行的办法并举,找出它们之间的数学差异。 显示一个可行 和一个诱惑 选择在这里失败, 然后解释决定性的区别。 你能比较一下目前决定的两个可能的选择,并解释为什么结果不同? 不要仅仅提出正确的路线;把它与一种可行的替代办法作对比,并说出他们分歧的确切地点。 给我两个本地的选项 来解释选择一个的属性

For each reply, first use this tagged section: <reasoning> your private thinking about what the student needs next </reasoning> Then use exactly one of: <output> your non-empty message shown to the student </output> <end></end> Use <end></end> when you think the conversation can end early. The student will see only the text inside <output>…</output>. Put all private thinking inside <reasoning>…</reasoning>. Do not use JSON or Markdown code fences. Do not reveal the problem’s answer or an equivalent expression to the student.
blocks.zh: 开始辅导( 用户消息) 现在你可以开始跟学生谈话了 对于每一份答复,首先使用此标记部分: " 解释 " 。 您对学生接下来需要什么的私人思考 </解释 > 然后准确使用: < 输出> 您向学生显示的非空信件 </ 输出 > < end%%/ end> 在您认为对话可以提前结束时使用"endQQ/end". 学生将只看到 < 输出 > ... < / 输出 > 中的文本 。 将所有私人思维放入 " 理性 " ... " / " 理性 " 。 不要使用 JSON 或 Markdown 代码栅栏。 请勿向学生透露问题答案或同等表达。

blocks.en: Earlier teacher replies retain their visible output, with private reasoning replaced by the following placeholder.
blocks.zh: 更早的教师回复保留了可见的输出,私人推理被以下占位符所取而代之.

blocks.zh: 早前教师回答"解释"(您先前的私人推理,本笔录中省略了) </解释 > < 输出 > {可见} </输出 >

blocks.en: The student uses the system message below during tutoring and testing. Tutoring inputs contain accepted exchanges and the current accepted teacher reply. blocks.zh: 学生在辅导和测试时使用下面的系统消息. 教学投入包含接受的交流和目前接受的教师答复。 辅导后,测试请求会附在被接受的对话后. 无辅助基线使用相同的系统消息并测试请求,没有交互历史.

blocks.zh: 学生系统消息 你是Sam,一个跟老师说话的学生。

blocks.en: Student testing request (user message) Now try to solve the problem from scratch: {{task }} Put your final answer in \boxed{}.
blocks.zh: 学生测试请求( 用户信息) 现在试着从零开始解决问题: 任务 将最后的答案放入\boxed 。

blocks.zh: D.3.1 答复正确性法官

blocks.en: The auxiliary answer judge compares the extracted student answer with the reference answer using the following messages.

blocks.zh: 回答法官:系统消息 你是一个严格的数学答案等同法官。 只将学生的解答与特定任务的地面真相解答相提并论. 只有在数学上等同的最后答案时,标记才正确。 返回有效的 JSON 只使用正确的密钥( boolean) 。

Ignore superficial notation differences, such as including the function name on the left side of an equation, when the right-hand side is equivalent. Do not use any hidden student reasoning. Return JSON only with this schema: { ”correct”: true or false }
blocks.zh: 答题裁判:用户模板 任务 : 任务 : 地面真相 : 地上真相 : 地上真相 被摘录的学生回答 : “ 摘录的” 回答 或 “ (空) ” 。 决定取出的学生答案在数学上是否等同于地面真理作为任务的最后答案. 忽略表面标记差异,例如当右侧相等时,在方程左侧包含函数名. 不要使用任何隐藏的学生推理。 返回 JSON 只使用此方案 : { “ 更正” : 真假 }

blocks.zh: 子目标分解学生希望老师解释下个目标是什么,为什么这有帮助

blocks.zh: 对比比较 学生希望老师列出不同的方法

blocks.en: Final user instruction Please reply in a few short sentences so that you do not overwhelm the student. Check the student’s last message, and if there is a problem with it, correct it first.
blocks.zh: 最后用户指示 请以短句回答,以免压倒学生. 校对:Soup

blocks.zh: D.4.3 注释说明

blocks.en: Annotators see the dialogue and the two student-visible teacher replies in randomized A/B order. They receive the following instructions and questions.
blocks.zh: 注释者以随机化的A/B顺序看到对话和两个学生可见的老师回答. 他们收到以下指示和问题。

blocks.zh: 任务介绍 您将读取数学辅导谈话,并比较两个辅导员的回答。 响应A和响应B的顺序按每个项目随机排列.

blocks.en: Task steps 1. Read the conversation and both tutor responses. 2. Compare the teaching quality of the two responses. 3. Briefly explain your choice. Please do not judge based on length, formatting, or other surface features alone.
blocks.zh: 任务步骤 1. 阅读谈话和两个辅导员的答复。 2. 比较两个答复的教学质量。 3. 简单解释你的选择。 请不要仅根据长度、格式或其他表面特征来判断。

blocks.zh: 优先权问题 什么反应能教学生更好? 答复A/答复B/大约相同

blocks.zh: 书面解释 你为什么选择这个选项?

blocks.zh: 确定学生最新尝试中的具体正确或错误部分,并解释原因。

blocks.en: Subgoal decomposition State the current subgoal, explain how it helps solve the problem, and work toward it.
